summary: Discovery to decide where to host embedding generation and rerank models. Customer evaluating Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pool vs Private VPC/on-prem. Primary concerns: 95th percentile tail latency for rerank, cost per 1M queries, data residency and KMS integration, and throughput scaling for batch embedding jobs. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark configs, and a private-deploy connectivity deep dive.
topics: vector DB integration (fanout vs local index)
transcript:
Header: 2028-04-17 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood), Dr. Sara Lin (CTO - NexisHealth), Marcus Hale (ML Lead), Anita Verma (Infra), Tom Ruiz (Product), Jing Park (Data Eng)

0:00 Alex Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from our side - I'm Alex, AE, Priya is our systems SE, Evan helps on benchmarks.
0:18 Dr. Sara Lin: Hi all, thanks. we'll be pretty focused, Marcus will cover the ML requirements, Anita our infra constraints.
0:30 Alex Morales: Great, goal of today's chat is to decide hosting approach for embeddings + rerank pilot and surface networking/security blockers.
0:45 Priya Kapoor: Quick agenda — current infra, embedding volumes/dimensions, expected qps and p99 SLOs, vector DB integration options, rerank placement, and next steps.
1:10 Marcus Hale: To give context — we run a search product for clinicians. Queries/day ~ 1.2M, peak qps around 140; expected pilot 200k/day but bursty. Typical query returns top 100 candidates from our vector DB then we do a rerank with a small 2B-ish model.
1:38 Alex Morales: When you say 2B-ish, is that an off-the-shelf model or custom? and is rerank done with the same embeddings or with separate features?
1:50 Marcus Hale: It's a fine-tuned open model — we currently run it on a single A10 box in prod for low-volume. Features: embedding dim 1536 (from our current encoder), some metadata features. We want the rerank to be fast — p95 under 120ms if possible.
2:12 Priya Kapoor: Ok p95 120ms is ambitious when you're doing a vector fanout plus rerank. Two general options: 1) embeddings and rerank served by Redwood near the app (hosted/dedicated) with local rerank to avoid network RTT to the vector DB, or 2) keep embeddings in customer VDB (Pinecone/Milvus) and call Redwood only for the rerank model or do hybrid — embed externally and rerank in Redwood.
2:42 Dr. Sara Lin: Security wise, we prefer data not to leave our region for PHI. So private or dedicated with VPC peering + KMS is preferable. Hosted API might be hard for compliance unless we have enterprise controls.
3:05 Anita Verma: Also, we have strict egress rules — any hosted option needs a clear list of IPs or private link.
3:18 Alex Morales: Understood. For dedicated we can allocate reserved GPU pools within a region and offer VPC peering; Private option provides a customer-managed control plane with on-prem or VPC deployment and brings KMS integration. We'll include SOC2 docs.
3:35 Tom Ruiz: Cost is big. For rerank, we care about cost per 1k reranks and cost per 1M embeddings. We're trying to model economics vs latency.
3:48 Priya Kapoor: Some quick numbers — if you quantize the rerank model to int8 or int4 we can reduce memory footprint and increase throughput by 1.8-3x, but there is a small accuracy impact; similarly embedding dims: moving 1536 -> 768 halves storage and retrieval costs but may change recall.
4:15 Marcus Hale: We did a quick A/B and 768 lost about 1.2% recall on our testset for top-10. Might be acceptable.
4:28 Evan Liu: For throughput, what matters is how you batch. If you do synchronous rerank per query with 100 candidates, batching across queries can amortize kernel launches. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching & KV cache for prefix hits which helps chat-like flows; for rerank the pattern is more bursty.
4:53 Marcus Hale: Our pattern is bursty; morning clinical hours are huge spikes. We need autoscaling that can handle 3x baseline for a 10-minute window.
5:06 Priya Kapoor: Dedicated pools support quick scaling and burst capacity; Private gives you control but autoscaling may depend on the customer's infra. We can pre-warm and keep a small committed pool to hit p95s.
5:28 Jing Park: For vector DB we currently use Pinecone managed; we'd either keep that or consider migrating to Milvus self-hosted if needed. How does Redwood integrate with an external vector DB?
5:45 Alex Morales: Two options: 1) Redwood calls your VDB as part of the pipeline (we call Pinecone for top K)** — this adds network latency; 2) you fanout vectors to both VDB and Redwood cache/index and run rerank locally in Redwood. Many customers do a hybrid where retrieval is done in VDB but rerank co-located.
6:09 Marcus Hale: If we keep the VDB external, what's a realistic p95 add?
6:16 Priya Kapoor: Depends on region and VDB average RTT; ballpark +30-80ms just for fanout roundtrips if cross-network. Coupled with rerank compute, could push p95 over 200ms.
6:30 Dr. Sara Lin: So for strict p95 under 120ms we probably must co-locate rerank with retrieval or keep a warm cache of candidates inside Redwood.
6:44 Alex Morales: Right — you can store a hot index or cache in Redwood via prefix/KV cache; or we can run embeddings + vector index on your private deployment so everything is intra-vpc with single-digit ms network calls.
7:03 Anita Verma: If we go private, how is KMS handled? We need to ensure keys never leave our KMS/HSM.
7:12 Priya Kapoor: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can keep keys in your cloud KMS; Redwood will not have raw key material. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
7:26 Marcus Hale: What's the deployment time for private vs dedicated?
7:32 Alex Morales: Dedicated reserved pools can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region. Private VPC deployment (managed) typically 4-8 weeks — longer if on-prem air-gapped.
7:45 Tom Ruiz: Timeline wise, we want pilot in 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
7:50 Alex Morales: Pilot in 6 weeks is tight but possible with dedicated + peering; private might be risky unless we start immediately.
8:03 Priya Kapoor: For a pilot we recommend starting with Dedicated — gives predictable throughput and easier onboarding. If compliance is strict we can do a dedicated in your VPC via peering, or start with dedicated and migrate to private later.
8:22 Marcus Hale: Sounds ok. For benchmarks — we want end-to-end: query fanout to top 100, rerank top 100 with our 2B model quantized to int8, 1536 embeddings. Can Redwood simulate that?
8:38 Evan Liu: Yes, we'll run a synthetic workload matching your histograms. We'll need the dataset sample and the spike profile. We'll test hosted vs dedicated vs private (if possible) but private will require your infra access.
8:51 Jing Park: We can share a 100k subset and traffic histogram. One caveat: our dataset includes PHI, so we need an NDA for data transfer.
8:59 Alex Morales: Noted — we'll use synthetic anonymized data for initial runs. For PHI we'll follow your compliance process; enterprise/legal already discussed NDAs previously.
9:12 Marcus Hale: Another question: vector dimension reductions — is there tooling to project to smaller dims on the fly?
9:20 Priya Kapoor: We don't do dimensionality reduction as a managed service but we can recommend approaches — knowledge distillation, PCA or training a new encoder. Many customers keep high-dim embeddings for recall and then use compact embeddings for latency-sensitive endpoints.
9:38 Tom Ruiz: Regarding rerank model size — are there options to split the model? e.g., two-stage rerank where a small model filters then a bigger model re-scores top 20.
9:48 Priya Kapoor: Absolutely, that's common. Two-stage reduces cost and latency; Redwood supports multi-model rollouts and routing policies, so you can run light model inline and heavy model for fallback / periodic re-score.
10:05 Dr. Sara Lin: What's the failure/fallback story? If dedicated nodes are saturated, do you fallback to hosted or a smaller model?
10:14 Alex Morales: We support graceful degradation policies: fallback to a smaller model or to an older model variant, and routing by latency policy; can also reroute to another region or capacity tier. We'll show examples in the runbook.
10:30 Anita Verma: Monitoring — what observability do we get? We need token-level latency + per-route P95 + audit logs for each request with request IDs.
10:42 Priya Kapoor: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token/latency breakdowns, trace hooks and 6 months of audit logs (longer retention as add-on). We can tie logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
10:57 Marcus Hale: How's the per-token pricing handled for rerank? If we do large rerank batches, cost could spike.
11:05 Alex Morales: Pricing can be usage-based plus reserved capacity. For rerank we meter token compute and model runtime. We'll include examples: cost per 1k reranks at different batch sizes, and committed discounts.
11:20 Tom Ruiz: Any caveats around embeddings stored in external VDB re: freshness and consistency?
11:26 Priya Kapoor: If you're writing embeddings to an external VDB there's eventual consistency and sync latency; for near-real-time you can write to both VDB and Redwood cache synchronously or use streaming replication. We have connectors/recipes for common VDBs.
11:44 Jing Park: On the topic of connectors, does Redwood do vector sharding or routing for high-throughput retrievals?
11:51 Evan Liu: Redwood doesn't replace your VDB sharding; we can operate with sharded VDBs and implement hybrid top-k routing. For rerank-heavy workloads we recommend sharding embeddings across dedicated pools and using consistent routing to reduce cross-node fanout.
12:09 Marcus Hale: curious about caching — can we keep a hot set of candidate vectors in Redwood to avoid VDB roundtrip for popular queries?
12:17 Priya Kapoor: Yes, prefix/KV cache for hot items is supported; works very well for repeated patterns. It reduces network roundtrip and significantly lowers p95 latency.
12:28 Dr. Sara Lin: Let's talk security specifics — SSO, RBAC, and audit — we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and role based access.
12:36 Alex Morales: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. We'll include our security pack with SOC2, ISO docs and the IAM mappings examples.
12:50 Anita Verma: For private we need to ensure no egress to internet aside from approved endpoints. How is software patching handled?
12:58 Priya Kapoor: For private managed we coordinate patch windows; we can do offline package delivery for air-gapped. For VPC you can restrict outbound and we provide a list of endpoints to allow for telemetry.
13:15 Marcus Hale: Ok shifting to cost modeling — Alex, can you walk through an example with our numbers?
13:20 Alex Morales: Sure — rough calc: assume 200k queries/day during pilot, top100 candidates, average rerank tokens 200, quantized int8; dedicated with reserved capacity gives X dollars per month — we'll attach a spreadsheet but short version: dedicated reduces per-call cost vs pure hosted at scale by about 20-40% depending on utilization.
13:43 Tom Ruiz: We need that spreadsheet. Also want to see committed capacity tiers and breakpoints where dedicated becomes cheaper.
13:50 Alex Morales: We'll send it.
13:55 Jing Park: For the benchmark, can you also include tail-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and warm vs cold start numbers?
14:04 Evan Liu: Absolutely; we'll run cold start, warm steady-state, and burst spike tests. We'll include CPU/GPU utilization and memory for the model variants.
14:18 Priya Kapoor: One more note on quantization — int4 is attractive but requires validation. Some models degrade more than others. We'll validate accuracy tradeoffs during bench runs.
14:30 Marcus Hale: Are there customers who've done a similar migration from Pinecone managed to Redwood private/dedicated?
14:36 Alex Morales: Yes, a healthcare customer migrated retrieval into a dedicated pool with VPC peering and kept Pinecone as cold store; they reduced p95 by ~60ms and cut per-query cost ~25%. We'll anonymize and share that case study.
14:51 Dr. Sara Lin: Good. Any blockers from our side for pilot?
14:55 Anita Verma: Need to verify outbound rules for peering and provide a SID for the network team. Also legal needs updated SOC2 docs.
15:04 Alex Morales: We'll send the SOC2, KMS guide, and network checklist tonight.
15:10 Tom Ruiz: Quick question — for experiments, can we do AB testing between reranking variants?
15:16 Priya Kapoor: Yes, Redwood supports canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback if the model underperforms; metrics tie into our evals so you can compare recall and latency.
15:30 Marcus Hale: Good. Regarding data residency, is dedicated deployed in multiple regions or single?
15:36 Alex Morales: Dedicated pools can be provisioned per region; for multi-region failover we set up cross-region routing and replicate models. For strict residency you can pin workloads to a specific region.
15:52 Dr. Sara Lin: Let's capture final decisions: for pilot we lean toward Dedicated in our region with VPC peering, quantized int8 rerank, keep embeddings initially in Pinecone but push hot set to Redwood cache, run benchmarks, then evaluate Private if compliance requires.
16:12 Alex Morales: Excellent summary — we'll create a pilot plan doc reflecting that and include timelines.
16:20 Evan Liu: Action items: we'll need the sample dataset, traffic histograms and infra constraints.
16:28 Jing Park: We'll provide dataset and histograms by Friday, and Anita will provide network rules.
16:35 Priya Kapoor: We'll prepare benchmark configs and propose test windows; expect a first pass within 5 business days after we have the data.
16:45 Alex Morales: Any other concerns?
16:49 Marcus Hale: Only that we validate the 1.2% recall drop if we try 768 dims in a side experiment.
16:57 Priya Kapoor: We'll include that experiment in the bench plan.
17:05 Dr. Sara Lin: Thanks everyone. We'll look out for the pricing and pilot doc.
17:12 Alex Morales: Thanks all — we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2, and schedule the deep technical VPC/KMS dive next week.
17:20 Meeting end.
